title: Strayhorn starts by writing out Duke's arrangements
summary: Strayhorn began copying out Duke's compositions when Tizol's extraction work became too much, learned how Duke worked and would not sell his secrets, which Duke liked.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What was the first number that Strayhorn did with the band? Was it a Strayhorn composition or did he start arranging Duke's compositions?

I think he started arranging Duke's compositions, writing them down, because Tizol used to extract all his arrangements and it was (like) getting) too much for him, so he decided to try the kid out and he liked what he did. And they got together and they used to put two and two together and find out that he knew more about what Duke was doing. And guys were trying to pay him to tell them the secret of Duke's arranging and he wouldn't do it, and that's why Duke liked him.
Was there a great similarity in their styles in the beginning or was that something that evolved through association?
